content: Should we do a Physlib conference? Online, or in person?
A message was moved here from #Physlib > channel events by Joseph Tooby-Smith.
@Fabio Anzà Moved this message to its own thread.
I would be very much up for something like this. I think in person would be great but even online would be good. I should have some research money available to help support this.
Awesome! I can also pitch in with some money
I guess the next questions here then are, when, where, how many people, how long?

How about the following

  • Where: Baltimore. We are between West-Coast and Europe. We have @Tyler Josephson ⚛️ here and, even if I don't know her, I'm hoping @Emily Riehl could be interested
  • When: How about the second half of December 2026, once the terms is over?
  • How many people: I would target something like 30/40. But I think we can accommodate much more with minimal organization
  • How long: I would do between 3 and 5 days. I feel 3 days is sort of the minimum for a technical workshop and longer than 5 days it'll probably start overlapping with people's additional academic duties

I’ll be on a research leave with Jeremy Avigad starting in September, so I’ll have time to focus on this, whenever / wherever it happens. I’ll be at CMU half of each week and in Baltimore half of each week.

In-person, one location is more convenient for organizers, and I’d like to meet y’all in person! It’s just more costly and less sustainable when folks need to cross an ocean. I would celebrate a Lean event in the US; I sometimes feel left out with all the Europe-located events I see advertised here.

I did participate in a Lean-for-teaching event which online, and that was nice and inclusive. But my goal for this event would be to actually bring Lean-curious non-mathematicians into the fold, and in-person would be a big lift there. Having hybrid option or at least recordings would help spread the word globally.

@Joseph Tooby-Smith, obviously @Tyler Josephson ⚛️ and I are biased towards UMBC and Baltimore. Since both of us are here, we can do most of the logistic lifting: Invitations, local logistics, setting up webpage and registration, lunch/coffee, social dinner etc.

Yeah, Baltimore sounds good to me. Unfortunately no matter where we choose there will be people who are unable to make it. But I agree that the benefits of in-person for this outweigh the downsides.

Just as a point of reference, my semester here would finish on 11th December, and I would likely be preoccupied until then. But also probably need to balance this with flight costs etc. which no doubt go up near the end of December.
We'll keep this in mind. Actually, it's very much aligned with the end of the term here. Something like 13-18 of December or so would fit well, I think
What will be the criteria for attendees as in the Minimum contribution criteria for the contributors to the repo??
I think we’ll allow zero contributions to the repo. (I for one, would like to attend :joy:)
I think speakers will be more established, but I’d like to open up attendance to domain scientists without much Lean experience, too
I know at some of these conferences, they do 'hackathon' type events - I would be up for something like this aswell if feasible.
I think that's a great idea!

Tyler Josephson ⚛️ said:

I think speakers will be more established, but I’d like to open up attendance to domain scientists without much Lean experience, too

I think I would reframe my question, I don't use Lean in my work and I'm not a scientist, I'm a semiconductor chip designer so I am irrelevant to the domain :sweat_smile: . That's why if contributors (regardless of background) can be allowed with a minimum number and quality of technical PRs, I can try doing that before December?? I can understand if the entry is still for those who are directly active in Lean, that would make sense so as to have only relevant network at the event

I applied for some money for a ~1 week workshop in Waterloo, CA, some time ago. I'd be interested in getting involved in something like this but I'd need it to be in Canada to do it in person
